long_biography.plain_text:
Stull began with a machine shop in Santa Fe Springs in the mid-1970s and expanded it into Tower Industries, an industrial group with metal-manufacturing operations in California and Wisconsin. He remains the company’s chief executive. Its Allied Mechanical business developed into a supplier of tooling, flight hardware, ground-support equipment and complex assemblies for major aerospace contractors.

Horse racing became Stull’s second long-term operating arena. He and his wife, Debi, established Tommy Town Thoroughbreds after buying a former training centre in California’s Santa Ynez Valley. The farm became a leading California breeder and produced or raced several graded-stakes winners. Stull later shifted the programme to a Kentucky farm, where breeding, raising, selling and racing remain the central activities.
